issues.quote: RouterBSI ensures non-decreasing empirical error on the retained set while bounding replay evaluation costs.
issues.problem: The sign is reversed; the statement also needs a fixed-current-replay qualification, not a global history or iterative validation guarantee.
issues.fix: Replace with: Including the unchanged predicate guarantees non-increasing empirical error on the current replay set under the recorded checker judgments; the cold-start gate does not guarantee monotonic validation or test performance. Match this scope in the title/abstract/intro and Figure 2.
issues.acceptance: Non-decreasing error is removed; the fixed-set/current-judgments scope is stated; no claim of global or test monotonicity remains.
issues.evidence: Main §4.2 p4 gives replay-risk <= old risk. A.2 p11 says global history is unbounded; A.4 p12 says cold-start gate is not monotonic against the previous predicate; G.1 p20 reports 262 retained decisions below previous predicate.

issues.problem: Main algorithm omits current-task inclusion and replacement semantics, and describes a tighter replay bound than the implemented current-inclusive set; decisive gate qualifications remain appendix-only.
issues.fix: State in §4.2 that two per-class histories have N=5 each, effective replay is their union plus current q (at most 2N+1), history uses uniform-slot replacement, and global seen-task storage is not bounded. Put Mp=3 and l=400 characters in §5.5. State end-of-pass per-skill rollback, rejection of ties/no validation support, and fixed cold-start comparator in §4.3.
issues.acceptance: Main equations and text agree with A.2/A.4/D.1; bounded means evaluation set, not all retained storage; default capacities and proposal count appear in main.
issues.evidence: A.2 p11 lines 836–874; A.4 p12 lines 902–929; Table 4 and D.1 p17. Main §4.3 strict inequality is already present, so do not claim it is wholly missing.

issues.quote: We split each dataset into train, validation, and test splits with ratios of 70%, 15%, 15%, respectively.
issues.problem: Main split description says per-dataset proportions; appendix says global constrained allocation and represented-skill evaluation, with substantial filtering.
issues.fix: Replace the per-dataset-ratio claim with global target allocation; give retained task count 4,987, split counts 3,491/748/748, gold vocabulary 306 versus 26,262 catalog skills, iterative rare-skill filtering, and explicitly state held-out tasks over already represented skills. Point to Table 3 for per-dataset counts.
issues.acceptance: No implication of unseen-skill generalization or identical per-dataset ratios; exact global counts and filtering scope appear in main.
issues.evidence: C.1–C.3 pp16–17 and Table 3; all three partitions contain every retained gold skill.

issues.quote: starting from the same initial predicates at iteration 0.
issues.problem: Figure 5 caption describes matched initial predicates, but G.1 says both-enabled uses three separately generated initial libraries and other configurations reuse the first; uncertainty terminology is also undefined.
issues.fix: Correct the caption to identify the actual initialization design, number of runs, task-weighting, and mean ± population SD. Distinguish Fig5 three-run means from Figs6/7 single-run values. For a causal matched-component claim, run paired initializations, otherwise qualify the ablation as not fully initialization-matched.
issues.acceptance: Caption matches G.1 pp20, Table10 p23, Table11 p24; plotted band statistic is named; no matched-initialization claim without matched artifacts.
issues.evidence: G.1 p20 lines1634–1638; Table10 shows different initialization means/SD; Table11 defines SD reconstructed from rounded variances.

issues.quote: MBR alone reduces token usage by 10.8%
issues.problem: A main-text efficiency comparison uses unmatched initialization cost and incomplete known-token accounts; decisive exclusions are only in the appendix.
issues.fix: Recompute a like-for-like optimization-only token comparison from the existing iteration column, or allocate the same initialization cost to each configuration. In §7.2/Fig6 explicitly label one run per configuration, known-only usage, omitted unknown attempts, and phase coverage. Do not call these per-query inference costs.
issues.acceptance: Compared token totals include identical phases and treatment of initialization; caption states the scope and unknown-use handling; percentages are recalculated.
issues.evidence: G.2 pp20–21 says only both-enabled includes local initialization and other runs omit external generation; Table12 p24 reports total, iteration-only and unknown attempts.

issues.quote: 94.68% of TheoremQA and 93.75% of MedCalc-Bench were cases where predicate failed to evaluate to true when the skill was required.
issues.problem: The frozen main text misinterprets extra-selection error shares as required-skill predicate-rejection rates and attributes them to narrow predicates; appendix explicitly denies this interpretation.
issues.fix: Delete the attribution and rejection-rate claim. Replace with the supplied-set facts from H.4: required skill present in 16/21 TheoremQA and 15/21 MedCalc-Bench task–retriever disagreement cases; extra non-gold slots can arise from top-five padding. Separate checker errors, predicate restriction, annotation mismatch and retrieval misses.
issues.acceptance: Main text matches H.4 pp26–27; 94.68/93.75 are not described as rejection rates, task rates or narrow-predicate evidence.
issues.evidence: H.4 p26 lines1910–1925 explicitly calls those archived extra-selection shares; H.3 pp25–26 contains clear evaluator errors.

issues.quote: predicates reach a plateau that cannot be overcomed with more capable LLMs
issues.problem: Three endpoint backbones, each with a single run, cannot establish an intrinsic ceiling or irreducible predicate-expressivity limitation.
issues.fix: Replace with: All three tested backbones improve over initialization, but final scores are not monotonic in model size; these runs do not establish a capability-independent ceiling. Reserve the expressivity hypothesis for limitations or test it via matched initialization/checker/proposer and repeated backbone runs.
issues.acceptance: Cannot-be-overcome and unsupported significance/causality wording removed; Fig7 clearly marks single-run results.
issues.evidence: Table14 p25 says each row is a within-one-run mean over 748 tasks. Main p7 itself notes Qwen3.8 has highest final score.

issues.problem: Figure 1 is a very small raster diagram with dense labels; it shows generic predicate routing rather than the replay-plus-gate contribution.
issues.fix: Redraw as vector at final 218pt column width with short task/predicate labels and visibly larger type. Optionally add a small failure→bounded-replay→gate cue or make the caption explicitly identify it as task setup; a teaser is editorial advice, not an ACL mandate.
issues.acceptance: All diagram labels can be read at 100% final-column view without zoom; no raster text required; figure/caption does not imply it demonstrates update control.
issues.evidence: Frozen p1 rendered image, actual image placement 218.25×59.18pt; raster 3098×840 pixels. High raster resolution does not cure tiny physical text.

issues.quote: Downstream success rates averaged equally across BM25, Vector, and SkillSight.

issues.fix: Use a zero-based bar axis or switch to a clearly labeled dot plot; increase labels to approximately 8pt at final size; state task- versus retriever-weighting, budgets k=5 vs SkillDAG k=10, and uncertainty availability. Rewrite caption final sentence without obscuring SkillDAG superiority.
issues.acceptance: Bar magnitudes are not visually truncated or chart becomes a dot plot; caption is grammatical and states SkillDAG is highest under its distinct budget.
issues.evidence: Rendered p6; chart vector text includes ~6.44pt labels, smaller subscripts; §5.5 p5 states different downstream budgets.

issues.quote: Routing failures drive revisions selected which are selected
issues.problem: Duplicated clause, lowercase bayes, and incomplete description of strict gate rejection weaken the main algorithm caption.
issues.fix: Rewrite caption: RouterBSI proposes predicate revisions after routing failures, selects a minimum-error candidate on bounded replay, and retains each changed skill only when its held-out error is strictly below its cold-start error. State end-of-pass gate timing, rather than implying a gate after each task.
issues.acceptance: No duplicate phrase; strict inequality/tie rejection and gate timing match §4.3/A.4; main diagram remains readable.
issues.evidence: Figure2 p3, §4.3 p4, A.4 p12; diagram already shows a strict passing example.

issues.quote: They are trained on training split and frozen on validation and test splits.

issues.fix: Give a compact per-method distinction between frozen pretrained/lexical retrievers, trained rerankers, and feedback-updated routers; identify what was fitted on which split. Remove the blanket trained-retriever statement unless verified.
issues.acceptance: Each baseline has one consistent training/tuning/freeze policy; no contradiction between §5.4 and §5.5.

narrative.title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Predicates for Skill Routing via Minimum Bayes Risk Replay and Held-out Gates
narrative.recoverable_thesis: Fixed-model natural-language applicability predicates can be improved from labeled routing failures via bounded empirical-error selection and a cold-start validation gate, preserving more required skills at small budgets.
narrative.abstract_notes: Thesis is understandable; roughly half the abstract motivates before naming contribution. 24.9% compares to cold start, while strongest learned-baseline comparison and downstream caveat are absent. Label gains relative and identify the represented-skill held-out setup. Word count is editorial, not policy.

narrative.related_work: Three-way nonparametric/parametric/static taxonomy is useful. Nearest identified analogue JTPRO is acknowledged at p2 lines141–145. Novelty is the combination of per-skill editable state, finite per-label replay and cold-start gate, not the mere presence of candidate evaluation/validation. Avoid blanket assertions all parametric methods need large data; quantitatively substantiate bounded-evaluation advantage with matched cost. Citation truth/coverage requires independent verification; no new missing citations fabricated.
narrative.conclusion: Frozen p8 explicitly says stronger routing does not consistently yield best downstream performance. Preserve this calibrated limitation; live source read differed, so do not critique frozen conclusion as omitting it.
